summary: Twenty-one scripts read per_pose_metrics.csv and seven scripts or notebook cells open <ID>_ligand.sdf directly. They fall into three classes. (1) Pure re-readers that gate on the column named `rmsd` (and `bestfit_rmsd` / `centroid_dist`): posebusters_validity_report, docking_effort_comparison, topk_recovery_gnina_arm, thesis_endpoint_diagnostics, optimization_benefit_stats, rank_success_analysis, ligand/receptor_docking_difficulty, diffdock_gnina_rerank_analysis (+chemotype), autodock_exhaustiveness_returns, filmstrip_rank1_top5_top15, interaction_pose_basis_audit (fig-14 join in pandamap_interaction_report too), boxed308_arm_compare. These need NO code change and re-run automatically IF the hub keeps the primary column named `rmsd` and moves rmsd, pb_rmsd, pb_kabsch_rmsd, bestfit_rmsd and centroid_dist to the SAME nearest copy (autodock_exhaustiveness_returns.py:570 asserts bestfit_rmsd == pb_kabsch_rmsd and the filmstrip pairs inplace=rmsd with form=bestfit, so a split convention breaks them). (2) Scripts with their OWN crystal logic that must be rewritten: pose_cluster_crystal_pocket_report.py (crystal_centroid at :921 loads the single instance; the "correct cluster" at :1109-1111 is the cluster nearest ONE crystal point within 4 A; every reach / co-reach / homogeneity / rank-in-cluster / precision@1 figure hangs on it; Table 3, Figs 5, 6, 38), run_pandamap.py (:963 fingerprints the single crystal instance on the reference chain; native recovery of a pose on another chain is 0 by construction because the key carries chain), pandamap_interaction_report.py (:1181, :1716, :2044 one native fingerprint per (protein, ligand); Table 4, Fig 7, figs 04-14), pocket_comparison_report.py (:1141 fpocket/p2rank DCC/DCA to the single crystal centroid), boxed308_raw_arm_metrics.py (:123, :67-84 duplicate scoring engine; measured inert at rank-1 on the boxed run). (3) Inert sites that only look relevant: run_posebusters.py :3522-3523 and Master_Docking cell[99] L81 use _ligand.sdf as a bond-order TEMPLATE (copy-invariant); Master_Docking cells [9] L221 / [13] L222 use it to define the OLD boxed search box (docking side, do not re-dock); _build_xray_control_notebook.py:283 busts the crystal ligand reference-free; rebust_hydrogen_normalised.py:254 reads only pb_valid; stats_utils.py, method_filter.py, pymol_pose_cluster_scene.py and all orai_* scripts carry no crystal reference. PoseBusters_DataSet_Analysis.ipynb cell[5] L12 already writes `n_instances` from _ligands.sdf into ligand_protein_features.csv, a ready-made single-/multi-copy stratifier. Derived new values from the six-arm nearest-copy table: docking_effort near2 pose counts 311->442 / 1622->2068 / 466->483 (AutoDock*/DiffDock*/EquiBind*); endpoint gate cost at rank-1 2/4/2 -> 2/5/2 complexes; difficulty-script single-arm oracle <=2 A 202->217 / 173->186 / 83->86 of 303; filmstrip 8 A trim keeps 190->249 / 164->224 / 143->155 PB-valid rank-1 poses; pose-level rank-1 4 A centroid reach 183->241 / 172->225 / 137->144. Everything cluster-level, PandaMap-level and form-level (bestfit vs the nearest copy) is "recompute".

Fourteen consumers then re-run with no code change, _RMSD_COLUMNS (validity_report:748), DEFAULT_RMSD_COLUMN (docking_effort:256), rmsd_col="rmsd" (topk:130) and the two synthetic tests stay valid. The one hard constraint is that every crystal-referenced column must use the SAME argmin copy per pose: autodock_exhaustiveness_returns.py:570 asserts bestfit_rmsd == pb_kabsch_rmsd and the filmstrip pairs inplace(rmsd) with form(bestfit).

decisions.question: How should pose_cluster_crystal_pocket_report.py define the 'correct' cluster when a complex has several copies?
options: Nearest cluster to the nearest copy (one correct cluster per complex, minimal code change)
Any cluster whose centre lies within --match-thr of ANY copy (several correct clusters; reach = a pose in any of them)
Keep single-instance clusters and report the nearest-copy reach as a separate column
decisions.recommendation: Option 2. It is the cluster-level analogue of per-pose min-over-copies and keeps reach, co-reach, homogeneity and rank_in_correct_cluster interpretable; purity and best_rmsd become per correct cluster. Option 1 would drop a tool's genuine recovery of copy B whenever another tool's cluster sits on copy A.

decisions.question: PandaMap native-interaction reference under nearest-copy?
options: Fingerprint every copy in run_pandamap.py and select per pose the copy given by a new nearest_copy_index column from the hub (Table 4 and Fig 7 recomputed)
Keep the reference-chain fingerprint and restrict figs 04-14 to poses whose nearest copy is the reference, disclosing the subset
Leave the interaction analysis on the single instance and state it
decisions.recommendation: Option 1 for a consistent primary endpoint; it needs the hub to emit nearest_copy_index and PandaMap to profile the copies against the canonical hetatm_cleaned receptor. Option 2 is the cheap fallback if the copies cannot be profiled on that receptor. Option 3 leaves interaction_pose_basis_audit's placement-share section internally inconsistent.

decisions.question: Which per_pose_metrics trees to rescore?
options: Canonical plus benchmark_full_protein_vina_scoring (Master_Docking cells 33/37/46/121-124) and the boxed benchmark tree (boxed308 A/B)
decisions.recommendation: Canonical plus the full_protein tree the notebook reads, so the two do not diverge in convention; the boxed tree is measured inert at rank-1 and can be left with a note, or rescored by boxed308_raw_arm_metrics.py for completeness.

decisions.question: Should pocket_comparison_report.py (fpocket/p2rank DCC/DCA to the crystal) adopt min-over-copies?
options: Yes, a predicted pocket on another copy is a correct pocket
No, pocket prediction is not a docking endpoint
decisions.recommendation: Yes if any of crystal_hit_matrix_*, crystal_top1_distance_ecdf or crystal_success_rate_table appears in the short build (check thesis_latex first); the change is a small loop and keeps 'crystal-referenced' consistent across the thesis.
